q: In the aml-alerts project, what is aml-xgb-v3?
a: The current AML alert priority ranker (2026-07-07), recalibrated on Jan-Jun 2026 dispositions. It orders the analyst queue and never closes alerts, and captures 96.3% of SAR-referred alerts in the top 40% on aml-oot-2026h1 (exp-407).

q: What came of the aml-alerts claim that the ranker captures 98.2% of SARs in the top 40% (aml-find-ranker-top40)?
a: It was overturned on 2026-05-15. Fresh dispositions on aml-oot-2026h1 (exp-405) showed aml-xgb-v2 captures 93.5% in the top 40%, and 96% needs the top 55%. aml-find-ranker-top40-revised replaced it, and v3 was recalibrated (exp-407).

q: What does aml-xgb-v2 use as inputs in the aml-alerts project?
a: aml-xgb-v2 uses feat-aml-structuring-v1, feat-aml-new-counterparty, feat-aml-round-amount, feat-aml-cash-velocity and feat-aml-kyc-band, trained on ds-aml-dispositions with cash features from ds-aml-cash-txn.

q: What is the current structuring-alert suppression rule in the aml-alerts project, and what sampling rate applies?
a: Structuring alerts scored below 0.18 by aml-xgb-v3 go to a 10% sampled review queue (dec-aml-suppress-018, carried into dec-aml-ranker-v3). The 10% sample was kept on 2026-08-18 (dec-aml-sample-10) after exp-408 found 1 SAR in 612 sampled alerts.

q: How many alerts and SAR referrals are in the aml-alerts holdout aml-oot-2026h1, and what top-40% capture does aml-xgb-v3 reach on it?
a: 9,870 alerts with 188 SAR referrals from Jan-Mar 2026. aml-xgb-v3 captures 96.3% of the SAR-referred alerts in the top 40% (exp-407, 2026-07-02).

q: Why does the aml-alerts ranker only reorder the queue and never auto-close an alert?
a: dec-aml-queue-only (2026-02-04): Omar Haddad (compliance) required that a model can prioritise but not close AML alerts, since closure needs an analyst disposition. The 94.1% structuring false-positive baseline (aml-find-fp-baseline) was handled by ordering, not closing.
